title: 1 Thessalonians
summary: 1 Thessalonians is a biblical book focused on faithful witness, holiness, resurrection hope, pastoral encouragement, and Christ's return.
historical_context: First Thessalonians encourages a young church to persevere in holiness and hope while awaiting Christ's return.
ancient_near_east_context: 1 Thessalonians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: 1 Thessalonians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received 1 Thessalonians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 8 of 13, 1 Thessalonians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting faithful witness, holiness, resurrection hope, pastoral encouragement, and Christ's return to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read 1 Thessalonians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: 1 Thessalonians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 8 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: 1 Thessalonians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: 1 Thessalonians anchors faithful witness, holiness, resurrection hope, pastoral encouragement, and Christ's return within Pauline Epistles, book 8 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul writes as founding missionary and pastor.
Christ's return shapes the letter's hope.
The church is encouraged to endure faithfully.

scripture_references.notes: resurrection hope and the Lord's coming

interpretive_notes.note: Read 1 Thessalonians first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
